_readme: Hand-curated media, keyed by pattern id from tools/lib/patterns.mjs.
Every playlistId here has been checked with `node tools/verify-media.mjs`,
which resolves it against YouTube's public playlist feed and records the real
title and channel. Only playlists owned by one of the four approved channels
are used: third-party mirror playlists resolve fine but can vanish or be
reordered by someone we do not control, so they are rejected on purpose.
kind: 'dedicated' = a playlist about exactly this pattern.
kind: 'course'    = a full DSA course that covers this pattern among others.
The UI shows that distinction rather than implying every link is dedicated.
Run `node tools/fetch-playlists.mjs` with a YouTube API key to discover
dedicated playlists for the patterns still on a 'course' fallback.

arrays-hashing.why: The A2Z course opens with arrays and hashing and builds the counting/lookup instincts the rest of the sheet assumes.
arrays-hashing.verifiedTitle: Strivers A2Z-DSA Course | DSA Playlist | Placements

two-pointers.why: Covered inside the A2Z arrays and strings sections, where two-pointer problems are introduced alongside the brute force they replace.
two-pointers.verifiedTitle: Strivers A2Z-DSA Course | DSA Playlist | Placements

sliding-window.why: The reference treatment. Builds one template, identifies which of four variants a problem is, then applies it — which is exactly how to recognise the pattern under interview pressure.
sliding-window.verifiedTitle: Sliding Window Algorithm | Face to Face Interviews

prefix-sum.why: Prefix sums appear in the A2Z arrays section, including the subarray-sum problems they exist to solve.
prefix-sum.verifiedTitle: Strivers A2Z-DSA Course | DSA Playlist | Placements

stack.why: Language-independent series covering implementation first, then the monotonic-stack problems that follow from it.
stack.verifiedTitle: Stack and Queue Playlist | Language Independent Series

queue.why: Same series — queues, deques and circular buffers are taught alongside stacks, which is how they are usually asked about.
queue.verifiedTitle: Stack and Queue Playlist | Language Independent Series

binary-search.why: The A2Z binary search section goes past sorted arrays into binary-searching the answer, which is where most of the hard variants live.
binary-search.verifiedTitle: Strivers A2Z-DSA Course | DSA Playlist | Placements

sorting.why: Java-native walkthroughs of each sort with the actual code, matching how these are written in this repo.

linked-list.why: The A2Z linked-list section covers traversal, reversal and the fast/slow pointer tricks end to end.
linked-list.verifiedTitle: Strivers A2Z-DSA Course | DSA Playlist | Placements

trees.why: Binary trees and BSTs from traversals through to lowest common ancestor, in both C++ and Java.
trees.verifiedTitle: Binary Trees | Binary Search Trees | C++ | Java | Data Structures and Algorithms | Placements

tries.why: Short, complete trie series — implementation then the prefix problems that justify the structure.

heap.why: Teaches heap problems by the signal that gives them away — 'k' plus 'smallest/largest' — rather than by the data structure.
heap.verifiedTitle: Heap Playlist | Interview Questions | Coding | Tutorials | Data Structures

recursion.why: Recursion by input/output trees and choice diagrams. The best available answer to 'how do I even see the recursive structure?'
recursion.verifiedTitle: Recursion Playlist | Coding | Interview Questions | Algorithm | Tutorials

backtracking.why: The same recursion series covers the choice-diagram method that every subset, permutation and board problem is built from.
backtracking.verifiedTitle: Recursion Playlist | Coding | Interview Questions | Algorithm | Tutorials

graphs.why: The most complete free graph series there is — traversals, cycle detection, then the algorithms. Interview-centric and Java-friendly.
graphs.verifiedTitle: Graph Series by Striver | C++ | Java | Interview Centric | Algorithms | Problems

advanced-graphs.why: The back half of the same series: Dijkstra, topological sort, union-find and minimum spanning trees.
advanced-graphs.verifiedTitle: Graph Series by Striver | C++ | Java | Interview Centric | Algorithms | Problems

dp-1d.why: The A2Z DP section works recursion to memoisation to tabulation to space optimisation in that order, which is the transition worth internalising.
dp-1d.verifiedTitle: Strivers A2Z-DSA Course | DSA Playlist | Placements

dp-2d.why: Grid and two-sequence DP — edit distance, knapsack, LCS — in the same A2Z DP section.
dp-2d.verifiedTitle: Strivers A2Z-DSA Course | DSA Playlist | Placements

greedy.why: The A2Z greedy section is deliberate about when the greedy choice is provably safe, which is the part that is usually skipped.
greedy.verifiedTitle: Strivers A2Z-DSA Course | DSA Playlist | Placements

intervals.why: Merge, insert and overlap problems sit in the A2Z arrays and greedy sections.
intervals.verifiedTitle: Strivers A2Z-DSA Course | DSA Playlist | Placements

math-geometry.why: The A2Z course opens with the maths and number-theory basics these problems reduce to.
math-geometry.verifiedTitle: Strivers A2Z-DSA Course | DSA Playlist | Placements

bit-manipulation.why: The A2Z bit-manipulation section covers XOR cancellation and masking, which is most of what gets asked.
bit-manipulation.verifiedTitle: Strivers A2Z-DSA Course | DSA Playlist | Placements

data-structures.why: Builds each structure from scratch in Java — which is exactly what the implementation files in this repo are doing.
